topics.name: Body & Medicine
topics.blurb: Organs, diseases and the people who cured them

topics.name: Cells & Evolution
topics.blurb: Cells, DNA, genes and how life changes

topics.name: Earth & Space
topics.blurb: Rocks, planets, stars and the deep past

topics.name: Ancient History
topics.blurb: From Sumer to the Middle Ages

questions.q: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.x: Beta cells in the pancreas's islets of Langerhans release insulin.

questions.q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.x: Babies start with around 270; many fuse together as we grow.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.x: The stapes, in the middle ear, is about 3 mm long.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.x: An adult's skin weighs around 4 kg.

questions.q: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.x: Red blood cells have no nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin.

questions.q: Which protein in red blood cells binds oxygen?
questions.x: Each haemoglobin molecule can carry four oxygen molecules.

questions.q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.x: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria on a culture plate he'd left out.

questions.q: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against which disease?
questions.x: In 1796 he used cowpox material; 'vaccine' comes from vacca, Latin for cow.

questions.q: What does a sphygmomanometer measure?
questions.x: It's the inflatable cuff used at check-ups.

questions.q: Which part of the brain coordinates balance and fine movement?
questions.x: The cerebellum holds more than half of the brain's neurons.

questions.q: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
questions.x: UVB light turns a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D.

questions.q: Scurvy is caused by a lack of what?
questions.x: Sailors on long voyages got scurvy until citrus became standard rations.

questions.q: Which blood type is the universal red cell donor?
questions.x: O negative cells lack A, B and RhD antigens, so most people can receive them.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.x: Two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it out.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.x: The thigh bone is roughly a quarter of a person's height.

questions.q: What do the kidneys' nephrons do?
questions.x: Each kidney has around a million nephrons.

questions.q: Which organ makes bile?
questions.x: The liver makes bile; the gallbladder only stores and concentrates it.

questions.q: Where are most nutrients absorbed?
questions.x: Millions of finger-like villi give it a huge surface area.

questions.q: What kind of organism causes malaria?
questions.x: Plasmodium parasites are spread by the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.q: Which of these can antibiotics NOT treat?
questions.x: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only work on bacteria.

questions.q: Hippocrates, the 'father of medicine', came from which civilisation?
questions.x: He lived on the island of Kos around 400 BC.

questions.q: Where in the body are alveoli?
questions.x: These tiny air sacs are where oxygen passes into the blood.

questions.q: What is the main job of platelets?
questions.x: Platelets are fragments of large bone marrow cells called megakaryocytes.

questions.q: What is the largest muscle in the human body?
questions.x: It keeps the body upright and powers climbing and standing up.

questions.q: What does an ECG record?
questions.x: Electrodes on the skin pick up the signals that trigger each heartbeat.

questions.q: Which hormone drives the 'fight or flight' response?
questions.x: The adrenal glands release it within seconds of a scare.

questions.q: Which gland produces melatonin?
questions.x: Melatonin rises in the dark and helps set the sleep cycle.

questions.q: The cornea is part of which organ?
questions.x: The clear cornea does most of the eye's focusing.

questions.q: Roughly how much blood is in an average adult?
questions.x: Blood is about 7% of body weight.

questions.q: Who performed the first human heart transplant, in 1967?
questions.x: Barnard operated at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

questions.q: Jonas Salk's 1955 vaccine protected against which disease?
questions.x: Salk didn't patent it, saying 'Could you patent the sun?'

questions.q: What is the medical name for the collarbone?
questions.x: It's one of the most commonly broken bones.

questions.q: Which organelle makes most of a cell's energy?
questions.x: Mitochondria have their own DNA, inherited from your mother.

questions.q: Where in a plant cell does photosynthesis happen?
questions.x: Chloroplasts descend from cyanobacteria swallowed by an ancient cell.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.x: They combine CO₂ and water into sugar, releasing oxygen.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of DNA's four bases?
questions.x: Uracil replaces thymine in RNA.

questions.q: Who wrote On the Origin of Species (1859)?
questions.x: Alfred Russel Wallace reached the idea of natural selection independently.

questions.q: Gregor Mendel worked out the rules of inheritance using what?
questions.x: He grew about 28,000 pea plants in his monastery garden.

questions.q: What shape is a DNA molecule?
questions.x: Watson and Crick published the double helix model in 1953.

questions.q: Whose X-ray image 'Photo 51' was key to finding DNA's structure?
questions.x: Franklin's X-ray crystallography showed DNA's helical shape.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are in a typical human body cell?
questions.x: That's 23 pairs: one set from each parent.

questions.q: Which type of cell division makes eggs and sperm?
questions.x: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and shuffles genes.

questions.q: Which part of the cell builds proteins?
questions.x: Ribosomes read messenger RNA and join amino acids in order.

questions.q: Bacteria are what kind of cell?
questions.x: Prokaryotes have no nucleus; their DNA floats in the cytoplasm.

questions.q: What is an organism's complete set of DNA called?
questions.x: The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs.

questions.q: Who first saw and described bacteria, in the 1670s?
questions.x: He made his own single-lens microscopes and called them 'animalcules'.

questions.q: Robert Hooke coined the word 'cell' while looking at what?
questions.x: The empty boxes in cork reminded him of monks' cells.

questions.q: What is water moving across a membrane toward the saltier side called?
questions.x: It's why slugs shrivel when salted.

questions.q: Which molecule do cells use as their energy currency?
questions.x: You recycle roughly your body weight in ATP every day.

questions.q: A group of similar cells working together is called a what?
questions.x: Tissues combine to make organs.

questions.q: Are fungi more closely related to animals or to plants?
questions.x: Fungi and animals share a common ancestor that plants don't.

questions.q: What is CRISPR used for?
questions.x: It was adapted from a bacterial defence system against viruses.

questions.q: What does RNA stand for?
questions.x: RNA carries genetic instructions from DNA to the ribosomes.

questions.q: Which human body part is a leftover tail?
questions.x: Human embryos briefly have a visible tail.

questions.q: Roughly when did life first appear on Earth?
questions.x: The oldest evidence is fossilised microbial mats called stromatolites.

questions.q: Ancient cyanobacteria filled the atmosphere with which gas?
questions.x: The 'Great Oxidation Event' was about 2.4 billion years ago.

questions.q: Bats and birds both evolved wings separately. What is this called?
questions.x: Similar problems often lead to similar solutions.

questions.q: What is an allele?
questions.x: Different alleles of one gene give, for example, different eye colours.

questions.q: What do enzymes do?
questions.x: Some enzymes speed up reactions by millions of times.

questions.q: Plant cell walls are mainly made of what?
questions.x: Cellulose is the most abundant organic polymer on Earth.

questions.q: A lichen is a fungus living in partnership with what?
questions.x: The fungus gives shelter; its partner makes food by photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which of these is usually NOT considered alive?
questions.x: Viruses can only copy themselves inside a host cell.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.x: Two pump blood through the gills; one pumps it around the body.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.x: Cheetahs reach about 100 km/h in short sprints.

questions.q: What is the largest animal alive today?
questions.x: A blue whale's heart is about the size of a small car.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.x: A parliament is owls; a pride is lions; a gaggle is geese.

questions.q: Which mammal can truly fly?
questions.x: The others only glide.

questions.q: Which land mammal has the longest pregnancy?
questions.x: About 22 months.

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs?
questions.x: Platypuses and echidnas are the only living egg-laying mammals.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.x: A newborn joey is about the size of a jelly bean.

questions.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
questions.x: Some hummingbirds beat their wings over 50 times a second.

questions.q: What are tardigrades also called?
questions.x: They can survive drying out, freezing and even the vacuum of space.

questions.q: Which animal has the largest eyes?
questions.x: Its eyes are about the size of a football.

questions.q: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
questions.x: Its fur hairs are hollow and colourless; they only look white.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.x: Spiders are arachnids, not insects.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an insect?
questions.x: Woodlice are crustaceans, related to crabs and shrimp.

questions.q: Axolotls are famous for being able to do what?
questions.x: They can even regrow parts of their heart and brain.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps around 18 to 22 hours a day?
questions.x: Their eucalyptus diet gives them very little energy.

questions.q: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe's neck?
questions.x: The same number as humans; each one is just much longer.

questions.q: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
questions.x: They spend up to 14 hours a day eating it.

questions.q: Whose blue blood is used to test medicines for bacterial contamination?
questions.x: Their blood clots in the presence of bacterial toxins.

questions.q: What is the largest living bird?
questions.x: Ostriches can be 2.7 m tall and lay the largest eggs of any bird.

questions.q: Which bird has the largest wingspan?
questions.x: Up to about 3.5 m tip to tip.

questions.q: What does a sea star NOT have?
questions.x: A ring of nerves around its mouth coordinates its arms.

questions.q: Which of these is a marsupial?
questions.x: Wombats are known for their cube-shaped droppings.

questions.q: What are sharks' skeletons made of?
questions.x: Cartilage is lighter than bone, which helps sharks stay buoyant.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat?
questions.x: Bears, pigs and humans are omnivores.

questions.q: Which is humans' closest living relative?
questions.x: Chimps and bonobos share about 98–99% of our DNA.

questions.q: What is unusual about male seahorses?
a: They carry and give birth to the young
They can live out of water
questions.x: The female deposits eggs in the male's pouch.

questions.q: Which big cat can purr but cannot roar?
questions.x: Lions, tigers, jaguars and leopards roar but can't purr continuously.

questions.q: How do dolphins sleep?
a: One brain half at a time
questions.x: The awake half keeps them breathing and watching for danger.

questions.q: Where does a flamingo's pink colour come from?
questions.x: Carotenoids in algae and shrimp turn their feathers pink.

questions.q: Which animal has the highest blood pressure?
questions.x: It has to push blood two metres up to its brain.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.x: A year on Mercury lasts 88 Earth days.

questions.q: Which is the hottest planet?
questions.x: Its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat at around 465 °C.

questions.q: Which planet has the Great Red Spot?
questions.x: It's a storm wider than Earth that has raged for centuries.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.x: So you always see the Sun as it was 8 minutes ago.

questions.q: What is the most common gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.x: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen.

questions.q: How old is the Earth?
questions.x: 13.8 billion years is the age of the universe.

questions.q: How old is the universe?
questions.x: Measured from the cosmic microwave background.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural mineral?
questions.x: Diamond is 10 on the Mohs scale; corundum is 9.

questions.q: Rock formed from cooled lava or magma is called what?
questions.x: Granite and basalt are igneous rocks.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.x: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.q: Which planet has the most spectacular ring system?
questions.x: All four giant planets have rings, but Saturn's are by far the brightest.

questions.q: Who was the first person in space, in 1961?
questions.x: His flight orbited Earth once in 108 minutes.

questions.q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.x: Apollo 11; the last crewed landing was Apollo 17 in 1972.

questions.q: Which theory explains how continents move?
questions.x: Plates move about as fast as your fingernails grow.

questions.q: Where is the deepest known point in the ocean?
questions.x: The Challenger Deep is nearly 11 km down.

questions.q: Which atmospheric layer contains the ozone layer?
questions.x: Ozone there absorbs most of the Sun's UV radiation.

questions.q: What causes Earth's seasons?
questions.x: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.

questions.q: What is at the centre of the Milky Way?
questions.x: Sagittarius A* is about 4 million times the Sun's mass.

questions.q: Which is the closest star to the Sun?
questions.x: It's about 4.2 light-years away.

questions.q: What does a light-year measure?
questions.x: It's how far light travels in a year: about 9.5 trillion km.

questions.q: Which planet spins on its side?
questions.x: Its axis is tilted about 98°, probably from an ancient collision.

questions.q: What is Earth's core mostly made of?
questions.x: The inner core is solid; the outer core is liquid metal.

questions.q: What was Pangaea?
questions.x: It began breaking apart about 200 million years ago.

questions.q: When did the (non-bird) dinosaurs die out?
questions.x: An asteroid impact at Chicxulub, Mexico, is the main suspect.

questions.q: What does the Mohs scale measure?
questions.x: Talc is 1, diamond is 10.

questions.q: Mars looks red because its surface is rich in what?
questions.x: Iron oxide is rust.

questions.q: In 1610 Galileo discovered four moons of which planet?
questions.x: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto are still called the Galilean moons.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.x: Fast enough to circle Earth about 7.5 times a second.

questions.q: What is the Sun mostly made of?
questions.x: About three quarters hydrogen by mass; most of the rest is helium.

questions.q: Which world was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
questions.x: Pluto hadn't cleared its orbit of other objects.

questions.q: Water vapour turning into liquid is called what?
questions.x: It's how clouds and dew form.

questions.q: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.x: Julius Caesar was a dictator, never emperor; Augustus was his adopted heir.

questions.q: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for which pharaoh?
questions.x: Built around 2560 BC, it was the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.

questions.q: The Rosetta Stone helped decipher which script?
questions.x: It repeats one decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek.

questions.q: The Code of Hammurabi comes from which civilisation?
questions.x: It set out 282 laws, including 'an eye for an eye'.

questions.q: Who invented cuneiform writing?
questions.x: Wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay, from about 3200 BC.

questions.q: The Greek and Latin alphabets grew from which people's alphabet?
questions.x: 'Alphabet' comes from alpha and beta, from Phoenician aleph and bet.

questions.q: Which city did Vesuvius bury in AD 79?
questions.x: The ash preserved the town, down to bread in the ovens.

questions.q: Who tutored Alexander the Great?
questions.x: Aristotle had studied under Plato, who studied under Socrates.

questions.q: Which Spartan king led the 300 at Thermopylae?
questions.x: Xerxes was the Persian king they fought in 480 BC.

questions.q: Which general crossed the Alps with war elephants?
questions.x: He marched from Spain to invade Italy in 218 BC.

questions.q: The Great Wall of China was mainly built to keep out whom?
questions.x: Walls were built and rebuilt over about 2,000 years.

questions.q: Which emperor was buried with the Terracotta Army?
questions.x: He unified China in 221 BC; over 7,000 clay soldiers guard his tomb.

questions.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still stands?
questions.x: It's also the oldest of the seven.

questions.q: Where did the ancient Olympic Games take place?
questions.x: At Olympia, from 776 BC, in honour of Zeus.

questions.q: Mesopotamia lay between which two rivers?
questions.x: The name means 'land between rivers' in Greek.

questions.q: Which civilisation built Machu Picchu?
questions.x: Built in the 1400s high in the Andes of Peru.

questions.q: What was the Aztec capital?
questions.x: Mexico City now stands on its site, on a drained lake.

questions.q: Who is traditionally credited with the Iliad and the Odyssey?
questions.x: Virgil wrote the Aeneid, a Roman answer to Homer.

questions.q: Herodotus is often called the 'father of' what?
questions.x: His Histories told the story of the Greco-Persian wars.

questions.q: In which year did the Western Roman Empire traditionally fall?
questions.x: 1453 is when Constantinople, the Eastern capital, fell.

questions.q: Which empire was ruled from Constantinople for about 1,000 years?
questions.x: Its people called themselves Romans the whole time.

questions.q: In which year was Magna Carta sealed?
questions.x: King John agreed to it at Runnymede, near Windsor.

questions.q: Who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
questions.x: Harold was killed; William became 'the Conqueror'.

questions.q: Which bacterium caused the Black Death?
questions.x: It killed perhaps a third or more of Europe in the 1340s and 1350s.

questions.q: Genghis Khan founded which empire?
questions.x: At its height it was the largest land empire in history.

questions.q: Where did the Vikings mainly come from?
questions.x: Today's Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

questions.q: Which civilisation built the city of Chichen Itza?
questions.x: On the equinoxes, shadows make a serpent appear on its pyramid's steps.

questions.q: Which Egyptian queen allied with Mark Antony against Rome?
questions.x: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid's construction.

questions.q: Archimedes supposedly shouted 'Eureka!' after realising what?
a: How to measure volume by displacing water
questions.x: The story says he worked it out stepping into a bath.

questions.q: Who brought movable-type printing to Europe around 1440?
questions.x: Movable type had been invented earlier in China and Korea.
